entries.name: Chest
entries.definition: Chests are interactable objects found throughout various areas that can be opened, broken, or activated to drop random or specific items.

entries.name: Low Mana
entries.definition: Low Mana is a condition that applies when the player's mana pool falls below 50%. However, it does not apply if the maximum mana is set to 0 due to Blood Magic.

entries.name: Low life
entries.definition: s.]] Low life is a condition that applies when life is at 50% or lower. Linking mana-reserving skills (such as auras) to which converts them into Life-reserving skills is one of the easiest way to maintain the low life condition.

entries.name: Luck
entries.definition: Luck is a mechanic that rolls an outcome or a number in a range more than once, with Lucky rolls applying the best result of two rolls, Unlucky rolls applying the worst result of two rolls, and Unexciting rolls applying the "middle result" of three rolls.

entries.name: Mace
entries.definition: Maces are a category containing two melee weapon item classes; One Hand Maces and Two Hand Maces.

entries.name: Maim
entries.definition: Maim, or the debuff name Maimed, is a keyword debuff that causes the affected target to have and has a default duration of 4 seconds. Maim is applied by attacks, just like hinder is by spells. It visibly appears as dark red pools on the ground the maimed entity stands on.

entries.name: Mana
entries.definition: Mana is a resource most commonly used to pay for skill costs. For the player it is shown as a blue orb in the lower right of the screen.

entries.name: Mana flask
entries.definition: Mana flasks are an item class and a subtype of flask which recovers mana over time. The flask end its effect if maximum mana is reached. They also queue up if multiple flasks are active.

entries.name: Mana before Life
entries.definition: Mana before Life is a game mechanic that allows mana to be used to take damage, increasing effective health.

entries.name: Cost
entries.definition: A cost is a property of skills. To use or trigger a skill, its cost must be paid. Most skills have a mana cost by default, though costs of life, energy shield, or rage are also possible. Reservations are not costs. Soul requirements for Vaal skills are not costs.

entries.name: The Maraketh
entries.definition: The Maraketh are a race/faction of Wraeclast. Their leaders are known as Sekhema. Their official language is "Marak".

entries.name: Marauder
entries.definition: The Marauder (known as Marauder of Ngamakanui from Nessa's dialogue) is Path of Exile's pure strength class, great at taking hits and better at dishing out punishment. His melee skills span the gamut from massive single target damage to devastating area of effect carnage. This colossus of a man bolsters his impressive physical arsenal with a variety of shouts and cries, skills that rally his allies and strike terror into the hearts of his enemies.

entries.name: Mark
entries.definition: Marks are a type of curse. Unlike Hexes, only one type of Mark can be applied at a time, and only to a single target.

entries.name: Relic
entries.definition: Relics are a type of item that is exclusive to the Sanctum league. They can be placed in the Relic Altar to provide buffs to various mechanics related to the Forbidden Sanctum.

entries.name: Annihilation's Approach
relatedTitles: First to Strike, Last to Fall

entries.name: Master
entries.definition: Masters are four special NPCs who are allied with the player and offer special missions during the Act campaign and inside maps, and can be invited to your hideout to interact with.

entries.name: Melee skill
entries.definition: Melee skills use melee weapons (axes, swords, maces, etc.) or the unarmed state to perform attacks. These skills have the Melee Gem tag.

entries.name: Melee weapon
entries.definition: Melee weapons are all weapons that don't launch a projectile with their basic attack. Melee weapons include swords, daggers, axes, claws, staves, maces and fishing rods. These weapons can be wielded to use melee skills.

entries.name: Mercenary
entries.definition: Mercenaries, or Mercenaries of Trarthus, are unique enemies introduced in Mercenaries league. Once encountered, a player can wager Gold to challenge them to a duel to take an item from them and hire them to assist the character. The Luminary ascendancy class for the Scion, with Noble Blood allocated, allows mercenaries to be hired permanently.

entries.name: Off-hand equipment
entries.definition: Off-hand equipment is a sub-category of equipment that are equipped in the off-hand slot (right weapon slot), typically alongside other weapons, to provide offensive or defensive benefits through modifiers.

entries.name: Crucible Passive Skill Tree
entries.definition: A Crucible Passive Skill Tree appears on weapons and shields that have been used in a Crucible Forge. After gathering enough experience from the Forge to unlock the first node, the item generates a random Passive Skill Tree that grants the item additional modifiers. An item can have up to five depths in its tree, and only one node can be allocated for each depth.

entries.name: Crucible Forge
entries.definition: The Crucible Forge is a mechanic that was accessible in areas in Crucible league that allows you to unlock and level up Crucible passive trees on a weapon or shield (or ).

entries.name: Mind Over Matter
entries.definition: Mind Over Matter (often referred to as MoM) is a keystone passive skill that allows the character's mana to absorb a portion of the damage dealt to life. It is the primary source of the Mana before Life mechanic for increasing effective health.

entries.name: Mine
entries.definition: A mine (or remote mine) is a type of proxy. Mine skills throw a device that uses that skill when detonated. Placed mines reserve mana while placed and most mines create an aura that affects nearby enemies.

entries.name: Shepherd of Souls
entries.definition: Shepherd of Souls is a keystone passive skill/keyword which causes non-aura Vaal skills to have significantly less Soul Cost but also increase their Soul Cost per Vaal skill used in the past 8 seconds.

entries.name: Minion
entries.definition: Minions are allied monsters summoned by the character. Minions have their own stats, and their actions are treated entirely separately from the summoner.
relatedTitles: Summon Greater Harbinger of the Arcane

entries.name: Mirage Archer Support
entries.definition: Mirage Archer is a support gem that causes linked bow skills to summon a ghostly archer. When the player hits an enemy with the supported skill, a temporary Mirage Archer is summoned above the player which uses that skill.

entries.name: Mirrored
entries.definition: Mirrored is a special property that appear on items created by a or a on a piece of equipment.

entries.name: Abyss jewel
entries.definition: Abyss jewels are a class of items that function similar to regular jewels. They can be obtained from Abyssal Troves and as an Abyss reward item from various other league mechanics.

entries.name: Modifier
entries.definition: Modifiers generally change various aspects of the entity they are affecting. Most commonly modifiers apply stats, however they can also apply buffs or grant skills and can often be found on items, monsters, strongboxes or areas.

entries.name: Molten Strike
entries.definition: Molten Strike is a strike (attack) skill that strikes an enemy, with some of the physical damage converted to fire damage. Each strike creates multiple molten ball projectiles that land to deal damage in a small area.

entries.name: Monster
entries.definition: Monsters are hostile creatures that reside in almost all areas, except for towns and hideouts. Slaying monsters is the primary source of gaining experience and a core aspect of Path of Exile.
relatedTitles: List of skills used by monsters

entries.name: Monster category
entries.definition: Monster categories are groupings of monster types that share a property. Some monster categories are used to populate maps with specific features. In rare cases, item or passive skill stats may behave differently based on the monster category or type being fought.

entries.name: Monster modifiers
entries.definition: Monsters can have modifiers alike items, strongboxes and areas. All modifiers can be divided into several groups: implicit, explicit (or affixes – prefixes and suffixes), torment and so on.

entries.name: Movement
entries.definition: Movement is a gem tag, usually describing skills that affect movement speed or are capable of moving the user as part of their effect.

entries.name: Movement speed
entries.definition: Movement speed (often referred to as MS) is a defensive stat that determines how fast an entity can move by running.

entries.name: Trauma
entries.definition: Trauma is a stackable buff that increases the damage dealt by , , and strike skills supported by .

entries.name: Blessing skill
entries.definition: A Blessing Skill is a gem tag for support skills that modifies the aura's reservation cost into something else. You can only have one aura on you from your Blessing Skills.

entries.name: Summon Sentinel of Radiance
entries.definition: Summon Sentinel of Radiance is a minion skill granted by Radiant Crusade, a Notable Ascendancy passive skill for the Guardian. It summons a Sentinel of Radiance that taunts on hit and deals fire damage over time to nearby enemies that scale with its maximum life. A portion of the damage you take is redirected to the Sentinel of Radiance's life pool while it's summoned. Only one Sentinel of Radiance may be active at a time.

entries.name: Summon Elemental Relic
entries.definition: Summon Elemental Relic is an triggered minion skill granted by Unwavering Crusade, a Notable Ascendancy passive skill for the Guardian. It has a chance to trigger when you or your allies kill an enemy or hit a rare or unique enemy.

entries.name: Tattoo
entries.definition: A tattoo is a type of currency item. They are applied to specific types of passive skills on the passive skill tree to transform the passive into a different one.

entries.name: Aspect
entries.definition: Aspect skills are granted by items. The skills reserve mana to provide various buffs in a similar way to heralds. Aspect skills are considered spells.

entries.name: Aspect of the Avian
entries.definition: Aspect of the Avian is an aspect skill that grants two buffs alternating every 4 seconds with each other with a cost of 25% mana reserved. The first buff grants you and your minions chance to deal double damage, and the second buff grants increased movement speed to you and your minions. Only one aspect skill can be active at a time.

entries.name: Aspect of the Cat
entries.definition: Aspect of the Cat is an aspect skill that grants two alternating buffs, each with their own duration. Cat's Stealth increases the character's stealth, gives a chance to avoid all damage from hits, and increases critical strike chance. Cat's Agility increases attack and cast speed. By default, their durations are 4 and 6 seconds respectively. Only one aspect skill can be active at a time.

entries.name: Aspect of the Crab
entries.definition: Aspect of the Crab is an aspect skill that generates a Crab Barrier every 0.5 seconds, granting physical damage reduction for each Crab Barrier the player has. All Crab Barriers are lost when the player takes physical damage from a hit. Only one aspect skill can be active at a time. The rate of Crab Barrier gain is unrelated to the skill's cooldown.

entries.name: Offering
entries.definition: Offerings are skills that consume corpses to buff the player's minions. Additional nearby corpses will also be consumed to extend the effect's duration.

entries.name: Oil
entries.definition: An oil is a currency item that can be acquired from Blight encounters. Using them on certain items gives these items an anointment, which can modify them in various ways.

entries.name: Aspect of the Spider
entries.definition: Aspect of the Spider is an aspect skill that applies a stack of on nearby enemies every second, increasing the damage they take by 5% per stack, and inflicts . Only one aspect skill can be active at a time.

entries.name: One-Handed
entries.definition: One Handed is a keyword which applies to the use of weapons which can take up the Main Hand or the Off Hand equipment slots.

entries.name: One-handed sword
entries.definition: One Hand Swords is an item class of one-handed melee weapons that require strength and dexterity and have a or implicit modifier.

entries.name: Event
entries.definition: Events (formerly races) are special short-term temporary leagues that players can participate in. Events often include additions and changes to the mechanics or gameplay loop to create an experience different from the base game. Events are occasionally held near the end of a challenge league's duration and often occur during winter months.
relatedTitles: Secrets of the Atlas Boss Kill Event

entries.name: Conversion
entries.definition: Damage taken as is sometimes referred to as conversion. While similar, it is a separate mechanic with different rules.

entries.name: Assassin
relatedTitles: Critical Strike Chance, Power Charge Duration

entries.name: Transfigured skill gem
entries.definition: Transfigured skill gems are alternate versions of existing skill gems, denoted by having "" as a suffix that alters its function and balance. While they are technically the same item as their default versions, they can often drastically change the identity of the skill, even changing its gem tags and mechanics.

entries.name: Tincture
entries.definition: A tincture is an item that can be equipped in a flask slot and activated to enhance the user's melee weapons with special bonuses. While active, they inflict Mana Burn on the user, causing mana loss over time at an accelerating rate, and will automatically deactivate when you reach 0 mana. By default, you can only have one tincture active at a time.

entries.name: The Viridian Wildwood
entries.definition: The Viridian Wildwood, also known as the Azmeri Wildwood or just Wildwood, is a league mechanic introduced in Affliction league. The Wildwood is a side area covered in darkness, where the player can explore a limited amount of space. Players can collect Wildwood Wisps that empower enemies in the zone once you leave it.
relatedTitles: The King in the Mists (Wildwood encounter)

entries.name: Eldritch
entries.definition: Eldritch is a monster category, as well as a property typically exclusive to monsters and bosses in the endgame of maps and the Atlas of Worlds.

entries.name: Penance Mark
entries.definition: Penance Mark is a mark curse skill that causes hits against the marked target to summon hostile phantasms. These phantasms can be killed by you.

entries.name: Overkill damage
entries.definition: The term overkill damage refers to a killing blow's damage in excess of the target's remaining life.

entries.name: Overwhelm
entries.definition: Overwhelm is a notable Ascendancy passive skill for the Slayer that sets the base critical strike chance of the equipped weapon to 8%, grants critical strike multiplier per nearby enemy, and lowers the critical strike multiplier of nearby enemies.

entries.name: Pain Attunement
entries.definition: Pain Attunement is a keystone passive skill that grants more spell damage when the character is on low life.

entries.name: Partying
entries.definition: Parties allow up to six players to play together. Players can create or join public parties by clicking on the Notice Board in a town, or by pressing S to open the Social window. Players can also invite someone to a party by selecting a player's name in chat, clicking on them in town, or typing /invite playername in the chat console.
relatedTitles: File:Dangerous Effects Mess Due To Party.jpg

entries.name: Runic
entries.definition: Runic monsters are encountered in Expedition. They spawn from the large skulls on spikes and have the Runic tag. In addition to being more difficult than regular monsters, they are affected by the modifiers of remnants which have been triggered before they spawned. Runic monsters also have Ward.

entries.name: Loss
entries.definition: Loss is a catch-all term for negative changes to resources, primarily life, mana, and energy shield. It can be considered the opposite of recovery.

entries.name: Passive skill
entries.definition: ]] The passive skill tree is a large network of passive skills, or nodes, that provide stats that affect the player's character (or their minions). All classes use the same tree, but start in different places. When a character levels up or completes certain quests, they gain one passive skill point, which allows the player to allocate a node on the skill tree that is connected to another allocated node.
relatedTitles: List of cluster jewel notable passive skills
The Master of a Million Faces

entries.name: Power
entries.definition: Power is a mechanic used to calculate certain skills and effects, primarily warcries.

entries.name: Chaotic Might
entries.definition: Chaotic Might is a buff that grants 30% of physical damage gained as extra chaos damage.

entries.name: Petrified
entries.definition: Petrify (or Petrified) is a debuff. Similarly to being frozen, petrified modifies the player's action speed by reducing it by 100%. Effects that prevent or minimize lowering of action speed, like Trickster's , Juggernaut's , , , or some Scourge modifiers, will prevent the player from being stuck in place and unable to use any skills. Petrified can only be removed by waiting out its debuff duration.

entries.name: Petrified Blood
entries.definition: Petrified Blood is a spell that reserves mana to protect the character's lower half of their maximum life by causing a portion of the immediate life loss from hits to be lost over time instead. At higher skill levels, the amount of life loss over time is reduced, even though the percentage of immediate life loss prevented remains constant. As a drawback, the character cannot recover life above low life by any means except with flasks and . Skills also gain an additional life cost while the character is above low life.
relatedTitles: First to Strike, Last to Fall

entries.name: Phasing
entries.definition: Phasing is a boolean stat. Phasing entities can move through enemies, but still obstruct the movement of enemies without phasing.

entries.name: Physical damage
entries.definition: Physical damage is one of the five damage types. It is the most common and the only one reduced by armour, rather than by a resistance. Most physical damage comes from weapon attacks, but some spells deal physical damage as well. Physical damage over time can be inflicted with the bleed ailment.

entries.name: Damage reduction
entries.definition: Damage reduction is a specific defensive stat most commonly granted by armour against physical hit damage.

entries.name: Pierce
entries.definition: Pierce is a behaviour of projectiles that enables them to pass through targets they hit, continuing along their original trajectory.

entries.name: Exerting
entries.definition: Exerting is a mechanic that allows skills to enhance subsequent attacks performed by the character. It is primarily associated with Warcries, though not exclusive to them.

entries.name: Point Blank
entries.definition: Point Blank is a keystone passive skill that scales the damage of projectile attacks with respect to the distance the projectile has travelled, increasing damage initially then reducing damage after covering a long distance.

entries.name: Poison
entries.definition: Poison is an ailment that deals chaos damage over time to the affected target.

entries.name: Moving
entries.definition: Moving is a keyword used in various stats. It is the opposite of being stationary. Movement speed affects the rate at which you move without the assistance of active skills. Teleporting refers to moving instantly.

entries.name: Retaliation
entries.definition: Retaliation is a gem tag associated with skills that become Usable when a certain condition is met, primarily blocking or taking damage. Retaliation skills can't be used until they become Usable, and have a cooldown once used. Because of their restrictive nature, Retaliation skills tend to have significantly higher damage stats.

entries.name: Gold
entries.definition: Gold is a collectable item that drops from monsters and loot containers that can be used to pay for various goods and services. Gold is not a tradable form of currency.

entries.name: Rune
entries.definition: Runes were currency items introduced in the Settlers league that can be spent to enchant non-unique weapons through Runesmithing. Runes can be obtained by shipping goods from Kingsmarch to the Kalguuran ports of Riben Fell, Pondium, or Kalguur. They can also be obtained by defeating a Settlers of Kalguur boss.

entries.name: Runesmithing
entries.definition: Runesmithing was a method of crafting that involves spending runes to add enchantments to your weapons at the Runesmithing Table in Kingsmarch or your hideout during Settlers league.

entries.name: Divine Blessing Support
entries.definition: Divine Blessing is a support granted by . It converts a supported aura skill into a Blessing skill, changing their Reservation to a one-time cost to grant the aura effect on duration with increased effect. You and your allies will only be able to benefit from one Blessing at a time per individual source.
relatedTitles: Category:Support effects not granted by support gems

entries.name: Portal
entries.definition: A portal is an entity that allows instant travel to and from the town in the Act where it is created (or the previous town if the current town is unvisited) and between a map and a hideout. The standard blue portal appearance can be changed by purchasing a Portal Effect.

entries.name: Power charge
entries.definition: Power charges are one of the three basic charge types. They are associated with intelligence and represent an increase to concentration and arcane energies during combat. They are visualized as glowing blue orbs surrounding the character. Gaining a new power charge resets the duration of all remaining power charges.

entries.name: Bloodsoaked Blade
entries.definition: Bloodsoaked Blade is a keystone passive skill that replaces Mana Burn and all related mechanics on tinctures with Weeping Wounds, draining life instead.

entries.name: Attack
entries.definition: Attacks are one of the main categories of skills, the other being spells. All attacks do damage, and some attack skills will also apply buffs or debuffs, or have other effects. The player's default attack is an attack skill that is always available to use.

entries.name: Prismatic
entries.definition: Prismatic is a gem tag. This tag applies to skills which choose a random element between Fire, Cold, and Lightning to deal damage with. This behaviour can be modified through Combat Focus jewels.

entries.name: Influence
entries.definition: Influence refers to monsters and items that have been empowered by powerful entities from the Atlas of Worlds. Influenced monsters can appear in maps that have had their influence drawn out by certain actions or modifiers, and may drop influenced items, special item bases that can roll modifiers not found on their normal counterparts. Maps can be affected by multiple influences, aside from their mutually exclusive counterparts.

entries.name: Profane ground
entries.definition: Profane ground is a detrimental ground effect that applies 100% increased critical strike chance and 10% increased curse effect against enemies standing on the ground.

entries.name: Projectile
entries.definition: Projectiles are entities that travel independently of their creator until they collide with an enemy or obstacle, or reach their travel distance limit of 15 metres. Skill gems that create projectiles usually have the Projectile or Bow gem tag.

entries.name: Puncture
entries.definition: Puncture is a bow attack skill that applies the Bleed ailment to enemies it hits, causing them to take physical damage over time that increases while the target is moving. Bleed applied with this skill deals more damage than usual.

entries.name: Attack speed
entries.definition: Attack speed is a property of attack skills. In combination with action speed, it determines the speed with which attack animations can be performed.

entries.name: Quality
entries.definition: Quality improves the signature stat of an item such as the physical damage on weapons and base defence rating on armours or adds additional bonuses to gems.

entries.name: Attribute
entries.definition: The three core attributes are Strength, Dexterity, and Intelligence. Most equipment, skill gems, and support gems have attribute requirements. A character must meet or exceed an item's attribute requirements in order to use it.

entries.name: Quiver
entries.definition: Quivers are a class of items that can be equipped in the off-hand slot while using a bow. Quivers are disabled and unequippable if a bow is not equipped.

entries.name: Races
entries.definition: Races are short-term events where players can participate and compete in a special temporary league to win prizes. With durations ranging from twelve minutes to one month, they allow players to demonstrate mastery and knowledge of the game in many ways. The goal is typically to accumulate the highest amount of experience possible or reach a certain objective within a time limit, starting with a fresh character and an empty stash. Many races have special rules, be it through special area modifiers or entire modifications to game mechanics and areas. Players receive reward points based on their placement on a race. Collecting enough reward points allows players to claim a unique item with alternate 2D art for Standard league.

entries.name: Rage
entries.definition: Rage is a counter utilized by certain attack skills and Ascendancy classes. Characters with Rage deal more attack damage — this affects the hit damage with attacks, but not ailments from the attack such as . This increases in magnitude with the amount of Rage accumulated. Rage rapidly depletes if you haven't gained Rage or taken a hit for 2 seconds.

entries.name: Rain of Arrows
entries.definition: Rain of Arrows is a ranged attack skill that fires a number of arrows in the air, which deal area of effect projectile damage as they land. Arrows initially fall at the targeted location, then spread outward.

entries.name: Raise Spectre
entries.definition: Raise Spectre is a minion spell skill that summons a defeated enemy as an allied minion.
relatedTitles: Guide:How to avoid losing your spectres

entries.name: Raise Spiders
entries.definition: Raise Spiders is a spell that summons two allied Spectral Spider minions per nearby corpse. These corpses will be consumed by this process.

entries.name: Raise Zombie
entries.definition: Raise Zombie is a spell that consumes a corpse to summon an allied zombie minion. Zombies are permanent minions with no duration that follow the user that summoned them.

entries.name: Rampage
entries.definition: Rampage is a kill streak mechanic that provides rewards for killing increasing numbers of enemies without stopping. The rampage effect is only available for characters equipping certain items.

entries.name: Range
entries.definition: The range of a skill or effect is the maximum Distance it can influence anything from its point of origin.

entries.name: Ranged skill
entries.definition: Ranged skills use ranged weapons (bows and wands), to perform attacks. The damage of these attacks is based on the weapons equipped.

entries.name: Ranger
entries.definition: The Ranger is Path of Exile's pure dexterity class, which befits her slim and graceful appearance. She is agile and fast, darting in and out of combat to deliver vicious critical strikes that often fell her enemies in a single blow. Her natural quickness grants her a profound ability to avoid damage through a high Evasion, and she tends to garb herself in light leathers and cloth. She has tremendous proficiency with ranged weapons, but she is as lethal as any man on the battlefield with a sword.

entries.name: Rarity
entries.definition: Rarity is a property found across different types of game content within Path of Exile, including most items, monsters, and strongboxes. The four rarities are , followed by , and . An associated game mechanic that determines the drop rate of higher rarity items is called "Item Rarity".
relatedTitles: List of items that alter Item Rarity

entries.name: Breach
entries.definition: Breach content involves otherworldly monsters who have stabilized their interdimensional rift to Wraeclast and have begun constructing hives throughout the land, first introduced in Keepers league. It is the sequel of the original Breach mechanic from Breach league.

entries.name: Foulborn unique item
entries.definition: A Foulborn unique item is a mutated version of an existing unique item that has one or more of its modifiers replaced with different ones. Foulborn unique items can be obtained from Breach related content, primarily the Genesis Tree using an or Grasping Coffers in Hive Fortresses.

entries.name: Hiveborn
entries.definition: Hiveborn are a species of monsters that are associated with Breach mechanic. They were introduced in the Keepers league and replacing the original Breach monsters in next leagues.

entries.name: Receiving damage
entries.definition: The following is an overview of most steps involved in damage calculations. Receiving damage involves several steps to determine whether the damage hits, how much damage is dealt by the attacker, how much of that damage is prevented by the defender's mitigation, and what resources (e.g. life, energy shield) are ultimately lost as a result.

entries.name: Recently
entries.definition: Recently is a keyword used in the description of various unique items, ascendancy skills, passive skills and enchantments. It refers to the past four seconds.

entries.name: Recoup
entries.definition: Recoup is a keyword mechanic that recovers an amount of life, mana, or energy shield over time, based on the damage taken from a hit.

entries.name: Recovery
entries.definition: Recovery refers to all positive changes to the current values of resources, most commonly life, mana, or energy shield. It is a catch-all term, not limited to specific mechanics. The opposite of recovery is loss.

entries.name: Regeneration
entries.definition: Regeneration is a form of recovery that automatically restores life, mana or energy shield over time.

entries.name: Sacrifice of Blood
entries.definition: Sacrifice of Blood is a keystone passive skill/keyword which causes life regeneration while at full life to give the user a Blood Barrier that can absorb damage from incoming hits, at the cost of halving the user's life regeneration rate.

entries.name: Beast
entries.definition: Beast (or "Animal") is a category of monsters that refer to animals and wildlife in Wraeclast.

entries.name: Summon Spectral Tiger
entries.definition: Summon Spectral Tiger is a skill that summons an allied Spectral Tiger minion for a duration.

entries.name: Mirage
entries.definition: Mirages, also known as "mirage areas", are a league mechanic introduced in Mirage league. Throughout Wraeclast, players can encounter a gateway to the Astral Realm, containing an imperfect copy of the current area holding a tortured captive djinn that must be released.

entries.name: Hallowing Flame
entries.definition: Hallowing Flame is a debuff that causes an attack hit against the affected target to gain 25% of physical damage as extra fire damage. Hallowing Flame cannot benefit the entity that inflicted it.

entries.name: Reservation
entries.definition: Reservation is a method of using a resource, typically mana or life, to pay for auras, herald skills, buffs, mine skills, or any skill with an ongoing effect. Some items may also reserve resources. Rather than paying the cost once as with normal skills, a portion of the resource is set aside as unusable for as long as the skill is active. Reserving a resource does not affect its maximum, so percentage modifiers such as are unaffected when you reserve life, for example.

entries.name: Resistance
entries.definition: Resistance modifies the amount of damage taken from elemental (fire, cold, or lightning) or chaos damage. It can be changed with equipment, passives, buffs/debuffs, and other modifiers.
relatedTitles: List of resistance related unique items

entries.name: Resistance penetration
entries.definition: Resistance penetration is a stat for hit damage that lowers the target's effective resistance to specific damage types for the purpose of damage calculations. The target's actual resistance value itself is untouched.

entries.name: Resolute Technique
entries.definition: Resolute Technique (often referred to as RT) is a keystone passive skill that will raise your chance to hit to 100%, ignoring all accuracy and evasion stats of the attacker and defender respectively, at the cost of preventing you from dealing critical strikes.

entries.name: Return
entries.definition: Return is a behaviour of projectiles that causes them to attempt to return to the entity that fired them after they collide with a target, terrain, or when they reach their maximum travel distance.

entries.name: Ring
entries.definition: Rings are a class of items that provide a variety of different bonuses when equipped. They are categorised as jewellery. Up to two rings can be equipped simultaneously. The Unseen Hand passive from the Nameless Bloodline grants a third ring slot, which is considered to be neither on the left nor right slot.

entries.name: Aura
entries.definition: An aura is a skill or buff that applies one or more effects on nearby allies and/or enemies within the aura's area of effect. This mechanic can be found on a variety of skills as well as NPCs and enemies.

entries.name: Pact skill
entries.definition: Pact skills are skills that empower specific types of spells, with the downside of inflicting an Affliction debuff on you. Currently, all pact skills are also exceptional skill gems.

entries.name: Brine ground
entries.definition: Brine ground is a beneficial and detrimental ground effect. Enemies on Brine Ground have 30% increased effect of Lightning and Cold Ailments on them and 25% reduced Armour and Evasion rating. Allies on Brine Ground gain 10% of Physical Damage as each of extra Cold and Lightning Damage

entries.name: Sapped
entries.definition: Sapped is an Elemental Ailment associated with lightning that causes the affected targets to deal up to 20% less damage, based on the amount of Lightning Damage in the hit, for 4 seconds.

entries.name: Savage hit
entries.definition: Savage Hit is a keyword that refers to hits that remove at least 15% of the target's maximum life.

entries.name: Sceptre
entries.definition: Sceptres is an item class of one-handed melee weapons that require strength and intelligence and have a implicit modifier.

entries.name: Scion
entries.definition: The daughter of corrupt nobles, the Scion was exiled to Wraeclast for killing her husband on their wedding night. She is aligned with all three core attributes - strength, dexterity and intelligence, which places her in the centre of the passive skill tree. This unique position allows her to develop into almost any type of character build, while lacking the dedicated specialisation that the other six classes offer.

entries.name: Scorch
entries.definition: Scorch is an Elemental Ailment associated with fire that causes the affected target to have their Elemental Resistances lowered by up to 30%, based on the Fire Damage of the Hit, for 4 seconds.

entries.name: Secondary damage
entries.definition: Secondary damage is a damage source that is not attack damage, spell damage, or damage over time. It hits.

entries.name: Secrets of Suffering
entries.definition: Secrets of Suffering is an item exclusive keystone passive skill. Upon taking it, the character will be unable to directly Ignite, Chill, Freeze or Shock enemies, but will inflict Scorch, Brittle, and Sapped upon a critical strike.

entries.name: Avatar of Fire
entries.definition: Avatar of Fire is a keystone passive skill that converts 50% of physical damage, lightning damage and cold damage to fire damage. However, the character cannot deal damage with any damage types except fire.

entries.name: Sextant
entries.definition: A Sextant is a currency item that can be used on a Voidstone to add a special modifier to maps.

entries.name: Shadow
entries.definition: The Shadow is Path of Exile's dexterity/intelligence hybrid class. He prefers to use fast-hitting weapons such as daggers or claws to dart in and out of battle, while laying traps or mines and controlling the flow of combat. He makes surgical use of offensive spells while dodging attacks, always outmaneuvering his opponents.
relatedTitles: the Belly of the Beast Level 1

entries.name: Avoidance
entries.definition: Avoidance is a keyword used to describe several different chance-based forms of mitigation against hits, certain types of damage, or debuffs or other mechanics.

entries.name: Shield
entries.definition: Shields are an item class of armour equipment. They can contain up to 3 sockets and need to be equipped in the off-hand slot. All shields provide a chance to block attacks, and some also grant implicit modifiers. Like Body Armour, shields have an inherent 3% movement speed penalty.

entries.name: Shock
entries.definition: Shock is an elemental ailment associated with lightning that causes the affected target to take increased damage from all sources. __TOC__

entries.name: Shocked ground
entries.definition: Shocked ground is a detrimental ground effect that inflicts a debuff that causing affected targets to take increased damage from all sources. Unless otherwise specified, it has a base Shock value of 15%.

entries.name: Shockwave Support
entries.definition: Shockwave Support is a support gem that causes the supported attack skill to trigger Shockwave on hit, damaging the enemy and enemies near it. It causes the supported skill to be restricted to staves and maces.

entries.name: Shrine
entries.definition: Shrines are special objects that apply an effect to nearby monsters or cast spells at nearby players. Interacting them allows the player to temporarily steal their power for themselves. This mechanic is also referred to as Domination.

entries.name: Silence
entries.definition: Silence is a curse that makes affected targets unable to cast spells or use warcries for 3 seconds. Attack skills can still be used.

entries.name: Sister Cassia
entries.definition: passive skill to an Amulet]] Sister Cassia is an NPC who introduces the player to Blight encounters. She can be found in The Sewers and The Imperial Gardens, as well as randomly in maps. After encountering her for the first time, she can be invited to your hideout.

entries.name: Skeleton archer
entries.definition: A skeleton archer is a type of undead monster (skeleton) found throughout Wraeclast that attacks with a bow.

entries.name: Skeleton
entries.definition: A skeleton is a type of undead monster found throughout Wraeclast that attacks with melee attacks.
relatedTitles: The Belly of the Beast Level 1
The Belly of the Beast Level 2

entries.name: Gem
entries.definition: Gems are a type of item that grants a skill (skill gem) or modifies a linked skill (support gem) when socketed into a corresponding socket in a piece of equipment. The character needs to have the required level and attributes specified on the gem to socket it. There are currently different skill gems and support gems in the game, for a total of .
relatedTitles: List of gems rewarded from quests
List of skill gems by gem tag
List of skill gems excluding vaal skills
List of skill gems granting vaal skills
List of support gems by gem tag

entries.name: Slayer
relatedTitles: Attack Damage, Frenzy and Endurance Charge Duration

entries.name: Smoke cloud
entries.definition: Smoke clouds is a detrimental ground effect that inflicts blind. The effect shared the same status icon name and graphic with ed, but with different text description.

entries.name: Snake
entries.definition: Snakes are a monster type found in acts 2 and 3 with a range of abilities.

entries.name: Axe
entries.definition: Axes are a one-handed and two-handed melee weapon class requiring strength and dexterity to equip. Most axes have no implicit modifiers but do have high base physical damage and moderate attack speed, resulting in overall higher damage per second than swords or maces.

entries.name: Soul Eater
entries.definition: equipped to steal the Soul Eater buff displaying how stacks increase character size.]]

entries.name: Spawn
entries.definition: Spawn is a spawn-type monster that are usually summoned by sea witches.

entries.name: Spell
entries.definition: Spells are skills that are cast or triggered by the user which can deal damage to an enemy or apply positive or negative effects to the caster, allies, or enemies. It is one of the two major categories for skills, the other being attacks. Unlike attacks, spells are not affected by accuracy or evasion.

entries.name: Split (item property)
entries.definition: Splitting items refers to the use of the Fenumal Plagued Arachnid beast, , or corpse modifier in the Necropolis to create a split copy of an item. This adds the split property to both copies, preventing them from being split again.

entries.name: Stat
entries.definition: Stats modify a single statistic of the game. Stats can apply to most aspects of the game, such as the player's character, items, monsters, skills or an area. Common sources of stats include modifiers, passive skills, buffs and skills.

entries.name: Statue
entries.definition: Statues are a monster type found throughout Act 3. They cannot be harmed, and block line of sight and projectile path, until woken.

entries.name: Staff
entries.definition: Staves are an item class of two-handed melee weapons that require strength and intelligence, as well as a moderately high base critical strike chance.

entries.name: Stealth
entries.definition: Stealth is a stat that makes it more difficult for monsters to see the character from far away. A character with increased stealth can get closer to monsters without them noticing.

entries.name: Abyssal socket
entries.definition: An Abyssal Socket is a special socket found on League-specific unique items and rare belt bases that can hold an abyss jewel.

entries.name: Strength
entries.definition: The strength attribute is a measure of a character's physical power. Strength is required to use strength-based equipment and skills.

entries.name: Strength of Blood
entries.definition: Strength of Blood is a keystone passive skill which disables recovery from non-instant Life Leech, while granting 2% additional physical damage reduction for every 3% recovery per second from life leech.

entries.name: Strike
entries.definition: Strike skills are melee skills which hit a single target or all enemies with a melee's swing radius. They are not the same as slam melee skills.

entries.name: Stun
entries.definition: Whenever a player or monster is hit, there is a chance they will be stunned. A stun interrupts whatever that creature was doing while a brief animation is played.

entries.name: Summon Bestial Rhoa
entries.definition: Summon Bestial Rhoa is a spell that summons an allied Rhoa minion. The skill is solely available through (Bestial Rhoa variant).

entries.name: Summon Bestial Snake
entries.definition: Summon Bestial Snake is a spell that summons an allied Snake minion. The skill is solely available through .

entries.name: Summon Bestial Ursa
entries.definition: Summon Bestial Ursa is a spell that summons an allied Ursa minion. The skill is solely available through .

entries.definition: Summon Greater Harbinger of Brutality is a skill granted by .

entries.definition: Summon Greater Harbinger of Directions is a skill granted by .
