aliases: Summon Greater Harbinger of the Arcane
entries.definition: Summon Greater Harbinger of the Arcane is a skill granted by .

entries.name: Summon Harbinger of Brutality
entries.definition: Harbinger of Brutality is a spell that summons an allied Harbinger minion. The skill is only available through .

entries.name: Summon Harbinger of Directions
entries.definition: Harbinger of Directions is a skill that summons an allied Harbinger minion. The skill is only available through .

entries.name: Summon Harbinger of Focus
entries.definition: Summon Harbinger of Focus is a spell that summons an allied Harbinger minion. The skill is only available through .

entries.name: Summon Harbinger of Storms
entries.definition: Harbinger of Storms is a spell that summons an allied Harbinger minion. The skill is only available through .

entries.name: Summon Harbinger of Time
entries.definition: Summon Harbinger of Time is a spell that summons an allied Harbinger minion. The skill is only available through .

entries.name: Summon Harbinger of the Arcane
entries.definition: Harbinger of the Arcane is a spell that summons an allied Harbinger minion. The skill is only available through .

entries.name: Ballista Totem
entries.definition: Currently all gems related to ballista totem have totem and projectile gem tags. Except , all gems also have the bow tag. All 3 ballista totem active skill gems are attack skills.

entries.name: Summon Raging Spirit
entries.definition: Summon Raging Spirit (commonly referred to as SRS) is a minion spell that temporarily summons a flying flaming skull that charges at enemies and attacks them.

entries.name: Summon Skeletons
entries.definition: Summon Skeletons is a spell that summons allied skeleton warrior minions.

entries.name: Summon Skitterbots
entries.definition: Summon Skitterbots is a skill which reserves mana to summon two invulnerable Skitterbot minions. The Skitterbots search for traps and mines you have laid and trigger/detonate some of them if an enemy is within targeting range. Mines detonated by Skitterbots are re-armed to detonate a second time. One Skitterbot has an aura that chills nearby enemies and the other has an aura that shocks nearby enemies. Skitterbots grant more trap and mine damage to the owner.

entries.name: Summon Spectral Wolf
entries.definition: Summon Spectral Wolf is a skill that summons an allied Spectral Wolf minion for a duration.

entries.name: Support gem
entries.definition: A support gem, or support, is a type of gem used to modify the stats and behaviours of compatible skill gems that it is linked to.
relatedTitles: List of support gems by gem tag

entries.name: Supreme Decadence
entries.definition: Supreme Decadence is a keystone passive skill which causes life recovery from flasks to also apply to energy shield, but reduces the recovery amount. Life flask effects are still removed on full life. The amount recovered is based on the life recovery, regardless of your maximum Energy Shield value.

entries.name: Supreme Ego
entries.definition: Supreme Ego is a keystone passive skill which increases your mana reservation amount, and prevents your auras from affecting allies, but grants increased aura effect to a skill per percent of mana reserved by that skill.

entries.name: Supreme Ostentation
entries.definition: Supreme Ostentation is a only keystone passive skill which allows the player to ignore Attribute Requirements (on the gems and equipment) and removes inherent bonuses provided by those attributes, thus making them irrelevant in most cases.

entries.name: Sword
entries.definition: Swords are a type of melee weapon that comes in three item classes: One-Handed Swords, Thrusting One-Handed Swords, and Two-Handed Swords.
relatedTitles: List of thrusting one hand swords

entries.name: Synthesised item
entries.definition: Synthesised items have their base implicit modifiers replaced with up to three Synthesis implicit modifiers. These are potentially very powerful modifiers that can't be obtained otherwise.

entries.name: Tailwind
entries.definition: Tailwind is a buff that grants the user 8% increased action speed for 4 seconds.

entries.name: Talisman
entries.definition: A talisman is a type of amulet. Talismans drop with an exclusive enchantment based on the item base. Talismans drop from Red and Unique Beasts from Bestiary encounters, and each talisman base drops from a specific kind of beast.

entries.name: Taunt
entries.definition: s]] Taunt is a debuff that makes an affected enemy unable to consider any object as a potential target, except the source of the debuff. It also causes enemies to deal 10% less damage to other entities. It lasts for 3 seconds. Taunt can be applied by players, minions, monsters, or proxies that are targetable (e.g. totems, but not traps, mines, or mirages). Taunt immediately expires when the character (or proxy) that applied it dies or expires.

entries.name: Banner
entries.definition: Banner skills are a sub-class of skills that can be manually activated to consume all Valour and place down a banner that provides an aura. The effect and radius of the Banner aura scales with the amount of Valour consumed. Valour is typically gained from melee combat.

entries.name: Templar
entries.definition: The Templar is a strength/intelligence hybrid character class.
relatedTitles: the Belly of the Beast Level 1

entries.name: Temporal Chains
entries.definition: Temporal Chains is a spell that curses all targets in an area, reducing their action speed and making all temporary effects on them expire more slowly.

entries.name: The Agnostic
entries.definition: The Agnostic is a keystone passive skill that removes your energy shield and drains mana per second to recover your life while you are not at full life.

entries.name: Barrage
entries.definition: Barrage is a ranged attack skill that fires all of your bow or wand projectiles rapidly in succession.

entries.name: The Impaler
entries.definition: The Impaler is a keystone passive skill. Whenever a hit from you or your skills impales a target, that hit also impales all nearby enemies, and applies an additional 5 impale debuffs to each (for a total of 6). It then causes each affected enemy to avoid impale for 5 seconds, during which impales cannot be Called from them with Call of Steel.

entries.name: Battlemage
entries.definition: Battlemage is a keyword. Battlemage gives the player character .

entries.name: Timeless Jewel
entries.definition: Timeless Jewel is the basetype of a set of six unique jewels that can alter the passive tree nodes.

entries.name: Tormented spirit
entries.definition: Tormented Spirits are a special type of undead monster. Once spotted, these apparitions of dead criminals flee from the player with their ill-gotten gains. When a tormented spirit touch another monster, it imbues them a with buff that increases their danger, but also their reward. When a tormented spirit touches a or monster, it possesses it and makes them even more powerful, but also makes them more rewarding. This mechanic is also referred to as Torment.

entries.name: Totem
entries.definition: Totems are a type of creature. They can appear as both monsters and as allies, and are a type of proxy when summoned by skills.

entries.name: Town
entries.definition: Towns are areas inhabited by NPCs, which serve as hubs for different areas of the storyline. Every act has one town.

entries.name: Transcendence
entries.definition: Transcendence is a keystone passive skill that causes armour to grant damage reduction against elemental damage instead of physical damage. It also lowers maximum elemental resistances.

entries.name: Trap
entries.definition: A trap is a type of proxy and skill behaviour, similar to totems and mines. Trap skills cause the player to throw a device that uses a skill, after being activated by a nearby enemy or by running out of trap duration.

entries.name: Travel
entries.definition: Travel is a gem tag. This tag generally applies to skills that assist with the character's positioning within the environment. Many Travel skills directly move the character to a designated location.

entries.name: Trigger
entries.definition: Triggering is a skill behaviour that causes a skill's effect to occur when a condition is met, instantly, without requiring a character animation. It should not be confused with trap activation, which uses the same word for a different mechanic (in English language settings).

entries.name: Bear Trap
entries.definition: Bear Trap throws a trap that deals physical damage to the enemy that triggered it and applies a debuff that greatly reduces movement speed and causes them to take increased damage from traps and mines.

entries.name: Two Handed
entries.definition: Two Handed is a keyword which applies to the use of weapons which take up both Main Hand and Off Hand equipment slots.

entries.name: Two Handed Melee Weapon
entries.definition: Two handed melee weapon is a keyword which applies to the use of melee weapons which take up both Main Hand and Off Hand equipment slots.

entries.name: Unarmed
entries.definition: Unarmed damage is a form of attack damage dealt by a character that does not have a weapon equipped. While it is unusual for most characters to ever use an unarmed attack, character builds based on unarmed damage can be made viable by using , , or Hollow Palm Technique. Though traditionally melee builds, ranged unarmed builds are possible with or .

entries.name: Unencumbered
entries.definition: A character or is considered unencumbered if their main hand, off-hand, and glove slots are all either empty or disabled. The unencumbered state is considered a stricter version of the unarmed state.

entries.name: Unholy Might
entries.definition: Unholy Might is a buff that grants 100% of physical damage converted to chaos damage, and 25% chance to inflict Withered on hit.

entries.name: Unique item
entries.definition: A unique item is an item with a specific name, unique artwork, and a predetermined list of modifiers. Unique items usually have the same implicit modifier as a normal item of the same type.
relatedTitles: List of unique items created with vendor recipes
List of unique items with custom effects
List of unique items with legacy variants
List of unique jewels received by corruption

entries.name: Unleash Support
entries.definition: Unleash Support is a support gem which causes the supported spell to generate Seals. Casting the spell will consume stored Seals to create additional skill effects in rapid succession.

entries.name: Unnerve
entries.definition: Unnerve is a debuff that causes affected targets to take 10% increased spell damage.

entries.name: Unwavering Stance
entries.definition: Unwavering Stance is a keystone passive skill that grants guaranteed stun avoidance, but prevents the character from evading attacks.

entries.name: Ursa
entries.definition: Ursae is a monster group (akin to subfamily of real world biology). According to the in-game Bestiary, it has two genera in-game: gargantuan and plummeting ursa. Ursae belongs to The Wilds family.

entries.name: Utility flask
entries.definition: Utility flasks are an item class and a subtype of flasks that provides a timed bonus effect over the flask duration.

entries.name: Vaal
entries.definition: Vaal may refer to: * The Vaal, an ancient race of Wraeclast * * Vaal Oversoul * Vaal skill * Vaal side area

entries.name: The Vaal
entries.definition: The Vaal are an ancient race of Wraeclast. All but 3,126 of the Vaal were killed by the Vaal Cataclysm instigated by the experiments of Doryani, Queen's Thaumaturgist and Atziri, last Queen of the Vaal. The survivors found refuge in the nearby Azmeri tribes, eventually entirely assimilating into their civilization. They were the first known users of gems and practised sacrifice.

entries.name: Vaal Pact
entries.definition: Vaal Pact is a keystone passive skill that grants instant life leech to melee attacks, but prevents all other forms of life recovery.

entries.name: Belt
entries.definition: Belts are a class of items that can provide certain bonuses when equipped. They are categorised as jewellery.

entries.name: Vaal skill
entries.definition: Vaal skills are granted by Vaal skill gems, a special type of corrupt skill gem that grants an alternative version of the skill with powerful added effects fueled by the souls of slain enemies, as well as the regular version of the skill.

entries.name: Accuracy
entries.definition: Accuracy is a property of attack hits. Together with the target's evasion, it is used to calculate an attack's chance to hit. Spells do not benefit from accuracy, as they cannot be evaded.

entries.name: Berserk
entries.definition: Berserk is a skill that applies a buff which grants increased rage effect. It requires rage to cast and expends rage while active. The effect lasts until you run out of rage.

entries.name: Veiled modifier
entries.definition: Veiled modifiers can be found on items, primarily those dropped by Immortal Syndicate members. The modifier will do nothing until it is unveiled by right-clicking the item. Unveiling the mod presents three random mods, and allows the player to choose which one the veiled mod becomes.

entries.name: Wand
entries.definition: Wands is an item class of one-handed ranged weapons that require intelligence, have a very high base critical strike chance, low base physical damage. While wands are more obviously suited for spells, they can be used and crafted for attacks.

entries.name: Warcry
entries.definition: Warcries are a type of skills that provide situational benefits to players while also taunting nearby enemies. Most warcries share the behaviour of buffing the user and nearby allies while also exerting a number of subsequent attacks, enhancing those attacks with additional properties.

entries.name: Ward
entries.definition: Ward is a defence capable of taking damage from hits before life or energy shield. It can only be found on item bases and uniques related to Expedition and Kingsmarch.

entries.name: Weapon
entries.definition: Weapons are a sub-category of equipment that are equipped to deal damage with attacks or provide various modifiers that modify a character's damage.

entries.name: Wicked Ward
entries.definition: Wicked Ward is a keystone passive skill that prevents energy shield recharge from being interrupted by damage if energy shield recharge began recently, but reduces your base energy shield recharge rate from 33% to 20%.

entries.name: Witch
entries.definition: The Witch is Path of Exile's pure intelligence class, making her an unmatched master of the elemental and dark arts. She wields the power of raw magic to decimate her foes from a distance. Her tremendous will surrounds her with a shimmering barrier against physical and magical attacks, a barrier that must first be pierced before the Witch herself is vulnerable. In addition to pure damage-based magic, the Witch can also cripple and kill her enemies with curses and diseases. She is a leery friend, and a dangerous enemy.
relatedTitles: the Belly of the Beast Level 1

entries.name: Wither
entries.definition: Wither is a channelled spell that applies the Hinder debuff, which reduces their movement speed, and a stacking Withered debuff, which increases chaos damage taken, in an area periodically while channelling.

entries.name: Withered
entries.definition: Withered is a debuff which applies a 6% increased chaos damage taken on the affected target, stacking up to 15 times. Each stack has its own independent duration (base duration of 2s), which is not refreshed when applying new stacks.
relatedTitles: File:2nd Screenshot of Withered (from Withering Step) in version 3.20.png

entries.name: Wrath
entries.definition: Wrath casts an aura that grants additional lightning damage to the attacks of the caster and their allies and makes their spells deal more lightning damage.

entries.name: Zealot's Oath
entries.definition: Zealot's Oath is a keystone passive skill that applies life regeneration to energy shield instead of life.

entries.name: Zombie
entries.definition: Zombies are a type of undead monster found in Wraeclast. They are found in various environments; some will emerge from the ground when a player is nearby. Zombies are typically slow and have delays between their melee attacks. Some zombies have special effects that occur on death.

entries.name: Bleeding
entries.definition: Bleeding, or bleed, is an ailment that deals physical damage over time to the affected target. Moving targets suffer increased bleeding damage. Only physical damage hits can inflict bleed. There are no sources of global chance to bleed or chance to bleed with spells. Thus, bleed is limited to attack skills only. Bleeding can be Aggravated to cause it to always deal damage as if the target is moving.

entries.name: Blight
entries.definition: Blight is a channelling spell that deals stacking chaos damage over time to all enemies in the area in front of the caster. Enemies who weren't affected by the damage over time are also hindered for a short duration.

entries.name: Blind
entries.definition: Blind (known as Blinded in status icon) is a debuff that lessens the accuracy and the evasion of the affected target by 20% and lowers visual light radius to its minimum.

entries.name: Blink
entries.definition: Blink is a gem tag. Blink skills have a shared cooldown; when one is used, all go on cooldown. All Blink skills are also Travel skills.

entries.name: Blocking
entries.definition: Blocking is a layer of defense that will entirely prevent damage from an enemy hit unless modified by some outside effect like . The chance to block is a random roll made for each hit. Characters and most enemies have 0% base block chance; enemies with a shield typically have some chance to block.

entries.name: Blood Magic
entries.definition: Blood Magic (often referred to as BM) is a keystone passive skill that changes all mana costs and reservations to life costs and reservations. It also grants more maximum life and removes your mana.

entries.name: Acrobatics
entries.definition: Acrobatics is a keystone passive skill that causes spell suppression modifiers to grant spell dodge chance instead, at half their value. Spell dodge prevents spell hits, and is capped at 75%.

entries.name: Body armour
entries.definition: Body armour is a type of armour equipment. Like shields, body armours have inherent movement speed penalties. In general, all STR and STR/INT body armours come with a larger reduced movement speed penalty and all other body armours have a smaller penalty.

entries.name: Action speed
entries.definition: Action speed is a stat that determines how fast or slow a character performs actions, such as running, swinging a weapon, casting a spell, or recoiling from being stunned.
relatedTitles: List of Searing Exarch implicit modifiers

entries.name: Boots
entries.definition: Boots is an item class of armour pieces that can contain up to four sockets.

entries.name: Bow
entries.definition: Bows is an item class of two-handed ranged weapons that require dexterity to equip. Quivers may be equipped with bows to provide additional bonuses. Bows have low base critical strike chance but moderate physical damage and attack speed, resulting in overall higher damage per second than wands.

entries.name: Skill
entries.definition: Skills, formerly referred to as active skills, are abilities actively used by players and monsters, unlike passive skills. Skills are typically gained by placing a skill gem into an item socket. Some items or passive skills may also grant skills through specific modifiers. Skills can be augmented with support gems or used indirectly through trigger mechanics.
relatedTitles: List of base items granting skills
List of modifiers affecting socketed gems
List of passive skills granting skills
List of unique items granting skills

entries.name: Brand
entries.definition: Brands are duration spells that create skill effects that can attach to an enemy. While attached, brands periodically 'activate', causing additional effects, usually dealing damage.

entries.name: Skill gem
entries.definition: Skill gem (known as Active Skill Gems in item filter), is an item class which grants skills to the player by placing them into an item socket. Similar to support gems, skill gems can gain experience and level up increasing both their Attribute(s) and character level requirement as well as the effect of the stats granted by the skill.
relatedTitles: List of skill gems by gem tag

entries.name: Brittle
entries.definition: Brittle is an Elemental Ailment associated with Cold. Hits against brittle enemies have up to +6% chance to critically strike afflicted enemies, based on the Cold Damage of the Hit that inflicted this ailment, for 4 seconds.

entries.name: Brutal charge
entries.definition: Brutal Charge is an alternative charge of . It's currently only granted from 's mod . Players can accumulate them the same way they generate endurance charges.

entries.name: Buff
entries.definition: A buff is an effect that can modify an entity's statistics, and can be identified by a green border around its icon. Buffs with primarily detrimental effects are debuffs and have a red border.

entries.name: Burning
entries.definition: Burning refers to any fire damage over time effect. Burning damage is a synonym for fire damage over time; all burning damage is fire damage over time, and vice versa.

entries.name: Burning ground
entries.definition: Burning ground is a detrimental ground effect that deals burning damage (fire damage over time). This effect is not the same as applying the ignite status effect. The amount of damage per second inflicted by burning ground depends on its source.

entries.name: Call of Steel
entries.definition: Call of Steel is a skill granted by , , , and , or unique items and . Using the skill generates Steel Shards that are consumed to empower those skills. It also pulls Steel Shards out of each nearby impaled enemies and corpses, dealing reflected physical damage equal to the total stored impale damage in an area of effect around them.

entries.name: Call to Arms
entries.definition: Call to Arms is a keystone passive skill which warcry skills to have more warcry duration, but causes them to no longer grant buffs or charges to the user.

entries.name: Carrion insect
entries.definition: A carrion insect is a type of beast monster found in and around Sarn and the Wetlands. Carrion insects have a distinct bulbous abdomen and swarm prey in large packs.

entries.name: Adrenaline
entries.definition: Adrenaline is a buff that grants increased damage, movement, attack and cast speed, and additional physical damage reduction.

entries.name: Cast speed
entries.definition: Cast speed is a keyword and refers to the speed of using skills which are spells and is calculated as uses per second. Casting a spell consists of cast time and other time mechanics and spell effect. Cast speed is calculated as 1 second/cast time of spell.

entries.name: Cast time
entries.definition: Cast time is a keyword and refers to animated action of performing skill and is counted in seconds. If cast time ends, effect of skill is started. Usually during skill effect next cast could be started.

entries.name: Catalyst
entries.definition: Catalysts are currency items that add quality to jewellery. Catalyst quality on jewellery improves the effect of the implicit and explicit modifiers of the specified type, depending on the modifier tags. Modifier tags can be viewed by enabling Advanced Mod Descriptions in the UI options, and then holding the Alt key (default, it matches the item highlight keybind) while mousing over the item.

entries.name: Aegis
entries.definition: An aegis is a type of skill and associated buff granted by certain items and Ascendancy passive skills. While active, the buff takes a specified amount of damage from hits (typically of specific damage types) before it is dealt to life or energy shield until it is fully depleted. The aegis will automatically restore to full after a skill-specific duration after either fully depleting the buff or not taking hit damage of the aegis' type for the same duration. Aegis skills' mitigation takes priority before Guard Skills.

entries.name: Caustic ground
entries.definition: Caustic Ground is a detrimental ground effect that deals chaos damage over time. The amount of damage per second inflicted by caustic ground depends on its source.

entries.name: Affliction charge
entries.definition: Affliction Charges are alternative charges of . They are currently only granted by 's mod . Players can accumulate them the same way they generate frenzy charges.

entries.name: Chain
entries.definition: Chaining is a behaviour of projectiles and chaining skills that causes them to bounce off their initial target and seek out another nearby enemy.

entries.name: Chainbreaker
entries.definition: Chainbreaker is a -only keystone passive skill. It grants rage regeneration based on mana regeneration, prevents mana recovery from regeneration, and adds a base cost of 3 rage to skills. Rage gained from this keystone does not delay inherent rage loss.

entries.name: Channelling skill
entries.definition: Channelling is a skill behaviour that allows a single use to last until the player releases its button, instead of finishing in one attack or cast time.

entries.name: Chaos Inoculation
entries.definition: Chaos Inoculation (often referred to as CI) is a keystone passive skill that grants immunity to chaos damage, but sets maximum life to 1.

entries.name: Chaos damage
entries.definition: Chaos damage is one of the five damage types. It is the rarest damage type and the hardest to get resistance against. Chaos damage bypasses energy shield, reducing life or mana directly. Although chaos damage reduction is based on resistance value, it is not considered elemental damage. One can become immune to chaos damage with the Chaos Inoculation keystone passive.
relatedTitles: List of enemies using chaos damage

entries.name: Character
entries.definition: A character is a player-controlled persona in the game with a unique name in the game world.

entries.name: Character size
entries.definition: Character size is a rare stat that alters the visual size of an actor's character model. This is a purely cosmetic function, and does not affect the character's collision radius or area of effect.

entries.name: Charge
entries.definition: Charges are counters that are represented as glowing orbs around an entity. They are not buffs.

entries.name: Chill
entries.definition: Chill is an elemental ailment inherent to cold that applies a slow effect to the character, reducing the animation speed at which the character plays. __TOC__

entries.name: Chilled ground
entries.definition: Chilled Ground is a detrimental ground effect that inflicts chill.

entries.name: Ailment
entries.definition: Ailments are a type of debuff associated and applied by one or more damage types. Ailments normally distinguish themselves from other debuffs by being applied by hits, which allows them to check conditions on the enemy, and vary their effect or duration based on damage instead of having a predetermined value from a skill or modifier.

entries.name: Claw
entries.definition: Claws is an item class of one-handed melee weapons that require intelligence and dexterity, have a moderately high base critical strike chance, high base attack speed and have a or implicit modifier.

entries.name: Close Combat Support
entries.definition: Close Combat Support is a support gem which grants the supported attack more melee damage based on how close the user is to the enemy. It also causes the skill to grant Combat Rush on hit, a buff which grants the next travel skill used within 2 seconds more attack speed. This support gem restricts the skill to swords and axes.

entries.name: Cluster jewel
entries.definition: Cluster jewels are a type of jewels that can be socketed in the outermost sockets of the passive skill tree (known as Large Jewel Sockets). These jewels extend the skill tree by creating new clusters of nodes, which can contain small nodes which can have their stats modified by the jewel, notable passives, and even keystones. They can also create more jewel sockets (Medium or Small Jewel Sockets) which can support smaller cluster jewels. They are occasionally dropped from Delirium encounters or rewards.

entries.name: Cold damage
entries.definition: Cold damage is one of the five damage types and is one of the three types which count as elemental damage.

entries.name: Conduit
entries.definition: Conduit is a keystone passive skill that shares charges with nearby party members only.

entries.name: Conflux
entries.definition: Confluxes are a family of non-stackable keyword buffs that make hits apply an elemental ailment, and allow all damage types to contribute to the magnitude of that ailment.

entries.name: Consecrated ground
entries.definition: Consecrated ground is a beneficial ground effect. The following effects are granted to those affected by it: * Regenerate 5% of maximum life per second * 50% reduced effect of curses on you

entries.name: Cooldown
entries.definition: A cooldown is a keyword property of skills. Skills with cooldowns cannot be used unless a cooldown is available. Once spent, a cooldown recovers over time.

entries.name: Corpse
entries.definition: Most creatures leave corpses on the ground when killed. Totems, shattered monsters, and enemies destroyed by certain effects cannot leave corpses.

entries.name: Corrupted
entries.definition: Corrupted is a special modifier. Corrupted items and strongboxes cannot be altered with most crafting methods, including restoration with an . There are limited ways to modify corrupted items.
relatedTitles: List of unique jewels received by corruption

entries.name: Corrupted Soul
entries.definition: Corrupted Soul is a keystone passive skill which causes 50% Non-Chaos Damage taken to bypass Energy Shield and grants 15% of Maximum Life as Extra Maximum Energy Shield.

entries.name: Crimson Dance
entries.definition: Crimson Dance is a keystone passive skill that halves the damage of bleeding, but causes hits to apply an alternative Bleeding debuff. Enemies take damage from up to 8 stacks of this debuff, but take no extra damage from it while moving. This effectively causes bleeding to be based on 35% of your flat physical attack damage per second, or 280% at 8 stacks.

entries.name: Ally
entries.definition: Ally refers to any creature on the player's side. They are subject to effects granted by equipment and skills, which have in their description "grants (effect) to nearby allies". Allies include: * Players in your party * Minions * Totems * Mirage Archers, Mirage Warriors, Mirage Saviours and Mirage Chieftains

entries.name: Critical strike
entries.definition: A critical strike is a type of hit that multiplies its damage by its critical strike multiplier.

entries.name: Crushed
entries.definition: Crushed is a debuff that lowers physical damage reduction by 15%.

entries.name: Culling strike
entries.definition: Culling Strike (also known as culling or cull) is a property that causes hits to kill enemies left with 10% of maximum life or less.

entries.name: Curse
entries.definition: Curses are a category of debuff, most of which can be applied by player skills. Curses are split into two categories: Hexes and Marks.

entries.name: Dagger
entries.definition: Daggers is an item class of one-handed melee weapons that require intelligence and dexterity, have a high base critical strike chance and also have a implicit modifier.

entries.name: Damage
entries.definition: Damage is the process by which a player or monster's life or energy shield is reduced.

entries.name: Damage conversion
entries.definition: Damage conversion is a mechanic that changes the damage type of a hit into another damage type. Damage conversions do not apply to damage over time.

entries.name: Damage effectiveness
entries.definition: Damage effectiveness is a property of skills that modifies the base and added flat damage of hits, primarily to prevent skills from benefiting disproportionately from flat damage. Low values of effectiveness are characteristic of skills that have high multipliers in other aspects of their damage application, such as a rapid hit rate or large damage modifiers.

entries.name: Damage over time
entries.definition: Damage over time (often referred to as DoT) is a damage inflicted continuously over a period of time. Unlike the other three damage sources, damage over time does not hit.

entries.name: Reflect
entries.definition: Reflect is a mechanic that causes an effect to act on its source in addition to its target. While damage is the effect most commonly reflected, curses and ailments can be reflected too.

entries.name: Damage taken
entries.definition: Damage taken refers to the amount of damage taken after all mitigations have taken place. It is a synonym of 'damage dealt', but from a defending standpoint.

entries.name: Damage taken as
entries.definition: Damage taken as, also known as damage shift, is a mechanic that allows damage from one damage type to be taken as another damage type. Most of these modifiers specify they only apply to hits; a few rarer sources also apply to damage over time. Damage shift is not conversion.
relatedTitles: File:Arrogance of the Vaal card art.png

entries.name: Alva, Master Explorer
entries.definition: Alva, Master Explorer (real name Alva Valai) is a master of Vaal heritage. She gives the player access to incursions, followed by the Temple of Atzoatl once enough incursions are completed. Players can encounter Alva from Act 7 onwards.

entries.name: Dance with Death
entries.definition: Dance with Death is a keystone passive skill which makes both Critical strike chance and damage with Critical strikes Lucky, at the cost of disallowing the use of Helmets and causing enemies' critical strike damage to be Lucky against you. Luck only applies to hit damage, not ailment DPS.

entries.name: Death
entries.definition: Death is a divination card. A set of four can be exchanged for .

entries.name: Death Aura
entries.definition: Death Aura is a spell that grants an aura that deals chaos damage over time around the user, like . It is granted by .

entries.name: Debilitate
entries.definition: Debilitate is a debuff that causes affected targets to deal 10% less damage and have 20% less movement speed.

entries.name: Decay
entries.definition: Decay is a debuff which causes affected targets to take chaos damage over time.

entries.name: Defences
entries.definition: Defences is a keyword that collectively refers to armour, evasion rating, energy shield, and ward. Armour, Evasion, and Energy Shield are sometimes referred to as the "Primary Defences" as they can be found globally throughout the game via equipment or the passive tree. Ward is a relatively newer type of defence exclusive to items found in the Expedition mechanic.

entries.name: Amulet
entries.definition: Amulets are a class of items that provide a variety of different bonuses when equipped. They are categorised as jewellery.

entries.name: Desecrate
entries.definition: Desecrate is a spell that summons corpses and a patch of desecrated ground, which deals chaos damage over time to enemies in the area.

entries.name: Desecrated ground
entries.definition: Desecrated Ground is a detrimental ground effect that deals chaos damage over time. The amount of damage per second inflicted by desecrated ground depends on its source. It is similar to caustic ground, which both deal Chaos DOT.

entries.name: Despair
entries.definition: Despair is a spell that curses all targets in an area, reducing their resistance to chaos damage.

entries.name: Determination
entries.definition: Determination is an aura skill that grants flat armour rating and more armour multiplicatively to the caster and their allies.

entries.name: Detonate Mines
entries.definition: Detonate Mines is a skill gem that performs the same function as the gem-less detonate skill that is automatically made available when a player has used a mine. Unlike detonating mines using the hotkey, the Detonate Mines skill gem can take advantage of mechanics afforded by being linked to support gems.

entries.name: Dexterity
entries.definition: The dexterity attribute is a measure of a character's agility and expertise. Dexterity is required to use dexterity-based equipment and skills.

entries.name: Difficulty
entries.definition: Path of Exile had three difficulties prior to The Fall of Oriath expansion: Normal, Cruel, and Merciless. Currently there's a single storyline playthrough, without players having to replay the same acts multiple times.

entries.name: Ancestral Bond
entries.definition: Ancestral Bond is a keystone passive skill that raises the active totem limit by one. As a drawback, the character cannot deal damage directly.

entries.name: Discipline
entries.definition: Discipline is an aura that grants energy shield to the caster and their allies.

entries.name: Distance
entries.definition: The base range of a melee weapon is displayed as a numeric value in its infobox with the label "Weapon Range". Additionally, modifiers to melee strike range are described as numeric values. Other than these, distances are not typically made known to the player through the game's user interface as explicit numeric values. In the few cases where a distance value is given, such as , that value is a measure of the radius of an area of effect.

entries.name: Divine Flesh
entries.definition: Divine Flesh is a keystone passive skill that causes you to take 50% of elemental damage as chaos damage and grants additional maximum chaos resistance, but causes all damage to bypass energy shield.

entries.name: Dodge
entries.definition: Dodge is a layer of defence that provides a chance to prevent hits.

entries.name: Dominus
entries.definition: Dominus, High Templar is the final boss of Act 3, found at the Tower Rooftop on the top level of the Upper Sceptre of God.

entries.name: Double damage
entries.definition: Double damage is an effect that causes a hit to deal double its damage. Double damage does not stack with and is overridden by triple damage.

entries.name: Drop rate
entries.definition: Drop rate describes the chance a certain source will produce items, most commonly killed monsters.

entries.name: Dual wielding
entries.definition: dual wielding two ]] Dual wielding refers to using a one-handed weapon in both hands.

entries.name: Duelist
entries.definition: The Duelist is Path of Exile's strength/dexterity hybrid class, making him unmatched at dealing and avoiding damage. He can effectively use a shield, but is equally comfortable slashing away with a powerful two-hander or fighting with weapons in both hands. His powerful arms can draw the strings of the heaviest and most lethal longbows. His highly honed reflexes give him a cat-like ability to dodge and parry incoming attacks, be they arrows or axe swings. The Duelist is a daunting foe, and his reputation as a ruthless killer is well deserved.

entries.name: Duration
entries.definition: Duration is a keyword that refers to the attribute of certain effects that continue over time, and specify how long the effect remains.

entries.name: Effect
entries.definition: Active and temporary effects can be placed on characters. strengthening or weakening the character considerably. They are shown on the top left corner with a short description when hovered over.

entries.name: Eldritch Battery
entries.definition: Eldritch Battery (often referred to as EB) is a keystone passive skill that makes energy shield protect mana instead of life.

entries.name: Elemental Equilibrium
entries.definition: Elemental Equilibrium (often referred to as EE) is a keystone passive skill. Whenever you deal any elemental damage with a hit, it applies fire, cold, or lightning exposure of the element(s) that the hit didn't deal the element of, and removes the exposure type of the element(s) that did.

entries.name: Elemental Hit
entries.definition: Elemental Hit is an melee attack skill that randomly deals fire, cold, or lightning damage in an area of effect around the target with each use. That use of Elemental Hit will only deal damage of the chosen element, and has more area of effect against enemies affected by the elemental ailments of that element. The skill deals more damage for each elemental ailment present on enemies.

entries.name: Elemental Overload
entries.definition: Elemental Overload (often referred to as EO) is a keystone passive skill that causes skills to deal 40% more elemental damage with hits and ailments for 8 seconds after that skill deals a critical strike, but prevents any interactions between critical strikes and ailments. When the damage multiplier is active for a skill, it is indicated by a diamond on the bottom of that skill's icon in the skill bar.

entries.name: Elemental damage
entries.definition: Elemental Damage refers to fire damage, cold damage, and lightning damage collectively. Passives or items which refer to elemental damage or elemental resistance will affect all 3 of these Damage Types or Resistances.

entries.name: Elemental proliferation
entries.definition: Elemental proliferation is a modifier that causes elemental ailments on an enemy to also affect nearby enemies.

entries.name: Elusive
entries.definition: Elusive is a buff which grants bonus movement speed and a chance to avoid damage from hits. It grants a large amount of avoid chance and movement speed when it is first applied, and the effectiveness of it decays over time. You must wait for Elusive to expire before you can re-apply it again at full strength.

entries.name: Endurance
entries.definition: Endurance is a notable passive skill that grants an additional maximum endurance charge.

entries.name: Anger
entries.definition: Anger is an aura skill that adds fire damage to the attacks and spells of the caster and their allies.

entries.name: Endurance charge
entries.definition: Endurance charges are one of the three charge types. They are associated with strength, and grant additional physical and elemental damage reduction. They are visualized as glowing red orbs surrounding the character.

entries.name: Enduring Cry
entries.definition: Enduring Cry is a warcry skill that taunts enemies in an area around the character, and grants the user and allies a life regeneration buff and a number of endurance charges, both based on the power of nearby enemies. Unlike most warcry skills, Enduring Cry does not exert your attacks.

entries.name: Energy shield
entries.definition: Energy shield is a form of defence that acts as an additional hit point pool on top of life. Along with armour and evasion, energy shield is one of the three defence types that can implicitly appear on equipment. Unlike life, energy shield will recharge naturally after the character has not taken any damage for 2 seconds.
relatedTitles: File:Start time of Energy Shield Recharge.png

entries.name: Enfeeble
entries.definition: Enfeeble is a hex spell that curses all targets in an area, lowering their damage and accuracy. Enfeeble does not reduce the damage taken from reflect, from a cursed enemy.

entries.name: Envy
entries.definition: Envy is a skill that grants an aura that grants added chaos damage for the attacks and spells of the caster and their nearby allies. Envy is not available as a skill gem - it can only be granted by modifiers on equipment.

entries.name: Animate Guardian's Weapon
entries.definition: Due to the wiki infobox coding, it is malformed. The mod is for the level 20 version of the skill, while is for the level 18 version.

entries.name: Ersi, Mother of Thorns
entries.definition: Ersi, Mother of Thorns is one of the tier 4 harvest bosses. It is the boss of "Wild" (purple) seeds.

entries.name: Animate Weapon
entries.definition: Animate Weapon is a spell that animates a weapon on the ground as a flying allied minion.

entries.name: Eternal Youth
entries.definition: Eternal Youth is a keystone passive skill which causes energy shield recharge to apply to life, but halves your life regeneration and life leech.

entries.name: Evasion
entries.definition: Evasion is the first layer of defence that affects a character's chance to evade incoming attacks. Evasion is opposed by the attacker's accuracy. Evasion is one of the four core defences that can appear locally on equipment, along with armour, energy shield and ward.

entries.name: Everlasting Sacrifice
entries.definition: Everlasting Sacrifice is a keystone passive skill that grants a temporary buff to maximum resistances when the character reaches full energy shield, then sacrifices all energy shield.

entries.name: Experience
entries.definition: Experience, commonly abbreviated to XP or EXP, is a game mechanic that allows characters to level up. When a character's current experience bar is full, they will level up, setting their current level's progress to 0%. Experience is primarily gained through killing monsters, though certain mechanics such as The Forbidden Sanctum, Trial of the Ancestors, and Betrayal encounters can also grant additional experience. Players can lose experience by dying, but cannot go below 0% experience or lose levels.

entries.name: Expiration rate
entries.definition: The expiration rate of a temporary effect describes how fast or slow time progresses for that effect relative to real time.

entries.name: Explode
entries.definition: Explode effects cause a killed monster or corpse to release an area of effect explosion, dealing secondary damage to nearby enemies, based on the monster's maximum life.

entries.name: Exposure
entries.definition: Exposures are debuffs that lower a specific elemental resistance.

entries.name: Fanaticism
entries.definition: Fanaticism is a buff that grants more cast speed, less cost, and increased area of effect for skills you cast yourself. It is exclusive to the ascendancy passive skill.

entries.name: Far Shot
entries.definition: Far Shot is a keyword that scales the damage of projectile attacks with respect to the distance the projectile has travelled, reducing damage initially then increasing damage after covering a long distance.

entries.name: Fire damage
entries.definition: Fire damage is one of the five damage types and of the three types which count as elemental damage.

entries.name: Fireball
entries.definition: Fireball is a spell that fires a projectile, dealing fire damage with an increased chance to .

entries.name: Fishing
entries.definition: Fishing is the activity of trying to catch fish. There are many Easter eggs in Path of Exile that are references to a running joke by Grinding Gear Games about the existence of secret gameplay features related to fishing. It has so far not been confirmed that any such gameplay features legitimately exist.

entries.name: Fishing Rod
entries.definition: Fishing Rod is a fishing rod base type. It is also the only fishing rod base type.

entries.name: Flask
entries.definition: A flask is a rechargeable potion. When used, the flask consumes a certain amount of flask charges and recovers a portion of life, mana or grants temporary bonuses for the duration of the flask effect.

entries.name: Fleeing
entries.definition: Fleeing is a status that causes enemies to attempt to run to a random point somewhere away from the player until they reach a certain point, are interrupted, or are unable to reach their selected point and give up. If a fleeing enemy becomes stunned, their fleeing behaviour will be interrupted. There is no fixed duration for fleeing.

entries.name: Flying
entries.definition: Flying is an inherent property held by certain entities and cannot be acquired by the player.

entries.name: Focus
entries.definition: Focus is a skill that grants the Focused buff. The buff does not do anything by itself, but certain veiled modifiers will grant bonuses while Focused. The Focus skill will automatically be granted to any character with an item with a modifier related to being Focused.

entries.name: Fork
entries.definition: Fork is a behaviour of projectiles that causes them to split into two identical projectiles when they hit a target.

entries.name: Fortification
entries.definition: Fortification is a stackable buff. Entities inherently have 1% less damage taken from hits per stack of Fortification. By default, it has a maximum of 20 stacks and lasts 6 seconds. The amount of stacks gained per hit depends on a combination of the hit's damage, the enemy's ailment threshold, and the enemy's rarity.

entries.name: Fractured item
entries.definition: Fractured items are of a special type of item base that have at least one affix coloured in gold () that is permanently fixed on the item. Items with fractured mod(s) can be dropped from rare monsters, rewards from various content, or created via using a Fracturing Orb.

entries.name: Freeze
entries.definition: Freeze (known in status as Frozen) is an elemental ailment associated with cold that causes affected targets to become frozen solid, preventing them from moving or using skills directly. Certain enemies cannot be fully slowed, but can still be considered frozen, which will result in them having significantly lower action speed.
relatedTitles: Abaxoth, the End of All That Is
List of monsters that cannot be fully slowed

entries.name: Frenzy
entries.definition: Frenzy is a ranged attack that grants frenzy charges on hit and also gains large bonuses from them. It requires a bow or wand.

entries.name: Frenzy charge
entries.definition: Frenzy charges are one of the three basic charge types. They are associated with dexterity and represent a temporary increase to swiftness and fervor during combat. The charges are visualized as glowing green orbs surrounding the character.

entries.name: Full life
entries.definition: Full Life is a condition that applies when the character's current life is at 100%. Full Life works when under the influence of Chaos Inoculation.

entries.name: Fungal ground
entries.definition: Fungal Ground is a ground effect that buffs allies and debuffs enemies. Allies gain 25% chaos resistance while on Fungal Ground, while enemies have all resistances lowered by 10%.

entries.name: Gain on kill
entries.definition: Life gain on kill, mana gain on kill, and energy shield gain on kill is a form of recovery that instantly restores an amount of life, mana, or energy shield respectively when the character kills an enemy. Regular on-kill gain only affects the character, and is not applied to or checked on other entities, such as minions, traps, mines, or totems.

entries.name: General's Cry
entries.definition: General's Cry is a warcry skill that taunts nearby enemies, and summons a number of mirage warriors from nearby corpses based on the power of nearby enemies and corpses. Mirage warriors perform one linked attack skill, then disappear.

entries.name: Ghastly Eye Jewel
entries.definition: Ghastly Eye Jewel is an abyss jewel base type. It is known as the "summoner" abyss jewel as it internally has a focus on summoner-related modifiers.

entries.name: Ghost
entries.definition: Ghosts have subtypes called wraith spirit, ghost pirate, ghost soldiers, and Dockhand Wraith (ghost that use bandit 3D model but only spawns in port areas).

entries.name: Ghost Dance
entries.definition: Ghost Dance is a keystone on the passive tree. It generates a Ghost Shroud every two seconds, up to a maximum of three Ghost Shrouds. When hit, a Ghost Shroud is removed and recovers energy shield equal to a percentage of your evasion rating.

entries.name: Ghost Reaver
entries.definition: Ghost Reaver is a keystone passive skill that causes the player to leech energy shield instead of life, and doubles the maximum total recovery per second from energy shield leech, with the downside of disabling energy shield recharge.

entries.name: Ghost Shroud
entries.definition: Ghost Shroud is the stack counter used by the Ghost Dance keystone.

entries.name: Glacial Cascade
entries.definition: Glacial Cascade is a cold spell that launches a wave of icicles. Damage from this skill converts physical damage to cold damage.

entries.name: Glancing Blows
entries.definition: Glancing Blows is a keystone passive skill which grants doubles both Attack and Spell Block chance while causing you to take 65% of the blocked hit's damage.

entries.name: Gloves
entries.definition: Gloves is an item class of armour pieces that can contain up to 4 sockets.

entries.name: Gluttony of Elements
entries.definition: Gluttony of Elements is a temporary aura that causes taking elemental damage to instead recover life for the caster and nearby allies. It can be obtained by equipping , which grants the level 10 version of this skill. (The skill level has no known effect.)

entries.name: Golem
entries.definition: Golems are a type of minion. Non-transfigured versions of golems provide a buff to its owner while alive (exception: Summon Carrion Golem); multiple copies of the same golem will not stack the buffs. A player can have a maximum of one active Golem by default.

entries.name: Grasping Vines
entries.definition: Grasping Vines is a debuff that reduces the movement speed of the character. Each stack is indicated by a vine that runs from the player to the floor, with the visuals changing based on the source of the debuff. Grasping Vines are elastic and will stretch while attached to the player. Each stack of Grasping Vines additively inflicts 8% less Movement Speed, up to a hard cap of 90% less Movement Speed. Most sources of Grasping Vines are capped at 10 vines (80% less Movement Speed), though different sources can stack independently.

entries.name: Vorana, Last to Fall
entries.definition: Vorana, Last to Fall is a boss that can only appear inside Expedition Logbook areas with zone level 68+ marked with Black Scythe Mercenaries.

entries.name: Uhtred, Covetous Traitor
entries.definition: Uhtred, Covetous Traitor is a boss that can only appear inside Expedition Logbook areas with zone level 75+ marked with Order of the Chalice. In addition, it is guaranteed to spawn if the logbook has the implicit for that area marked with Order of the Chalice.

entries.name: Ground Slam
entries.definition: Ground Slam is a melee attack creating a wave that travels forwards and damages enemies with an increased chance to stun.

entries.name: Ground effect
entries.definition: A ground effect is the general term for a patch of terrain that has some consequence on characters or monsters positioned on it. Burning ground created by the skill is one common example of a ground effect.

entries.name: Guard
entries.definition: Guard is a type of Blackguard which accompanies Guard Captain.

entries.name: Guard skill
entries.definition: Guard skills are active skills that provide defensive buffs for a short duration. Guard skills are all instant spells.

entries.name: Guardian

entries.name: Harbinger
entries.definition: Harbingers are a type of monsters that cannot be harmed directly. Harbingers summon enemies to fight the player while empowering them in different ways, and they can only be harmed by killing their minions. Harbingers can drop currency shards, for both ones seen in Wraeclast as well as their own exclusive currency.

entries.name: Stationary
entries.definition: Stationary is a keyword used in various stats. It is the opposite of moving.

entries.name: Version 3.16.0
relatedTitles: Heart of the Grove (atlas passive skill)

entries.name: Spell suppression
entries.definition: Spell Suppression is a type of mitigation associated with dexterity. By default, it provides a chance to lower the damage of hits and ailments inflicted by spells by 40%.

entries.name: Tornado
entries.definition: Tornado is a spell skill that creates a tornado which repeatedly damages enemies around it. It will move forward for a duration, during which projectiles from you (or your skills used by proxies) can collide with it to deal damage as though it was an enemy. Then it will chase down enemies for a secondary duration, and reflect a portion of the damage it took from projectiles, in addition to its own spell damage.

entries.name: Energy Blade
entries.definition: Energy Blade is a lightning spell that grants a buff which significantly lowers your maximum Energy Shield to transform your equipped weapons into Swords formed from that energy. Casting the spell again removes the buff. Requires all equipped weapons to be swords.

entries.name: Temporal Rift
entries.definition: Temporal Rift is a skill gem. It reserves mana to apply a buff that grants immunity to Temporal Chains and leaves afterimages in your wake, lingering for up to 4 seconds. Using the skill again will teleport you to the oldest afterimage, as well as reset your Life, Mana and Energy Shield to the values they had when that afterimage was created.

entries.name: Lethe Shade
entries.definition: Lethe Shade is a keystone passive skill which enables you to take 50% less Damage over Time if you've started taking Damage over Time in the past second, at the cost of having 100% more Duration of Ailments on you.

entries.name: Hatred
entries.definition: Hatred is an aura skill that grants the user and allies extra cold damage based on their physical damage.

entries.name: Helmet
entries.definition: Helmets is an item class of armour pieces that can contain up to 4 sockets. (Item level may affects the max socket, which can be bypassed by crafting bench recipe that change the number of sockets).

entries.name: Herald
entries.definition: Herald is a gem tag associated with active skills which grant the user both a damage buff and a special effect upon hitting or killing an enemy under certain conditions. Each Herald has a base mana reservation of 25%.

entries.name: Hexproof
entries.definition: Hexproof is a keyword and modifier that causes characters and monsters with it to be unaffected by Hex curses, but can be bypassed under certain conditions.

entries.name: Hinder
entries.definition: Hinder is a debuff that reduces movement speed on the affected target. A creature can only be affected by one Hinder at a time; if a creature is hindered by multiple sources, only the strongest Hinder takes effect.

entries.name: Historic
entries.definition: Historic is a keyword found on several unique jewels that have the ability to modify the passives found on the passive skill tree.

entries.name: Hit
entries.definition: The term hit refers to any damage that isn't damage over time.

entries.name: Hits can't be evaded
entries.definition: Hits can't be evaded (and its variations) is a modifier that can be found on weapons, skills and passive skills. It makes attacks ignore attacker's accuracy and target's evasion, for an effective 100% chance to hit a target.

entries.name: Hollow Palm Technique
entries.definition: Hollow Palm Technique is a keystone passive skill which grants various bonuses while the player is Unencumbered (being Unarmed with no off-hand or gloves equipped).

entries.name: Mastery
entries.definition: Masteries are special passive skills present on most passive skill clusters of the skill tree, which can be allocated after allocating a notable in their cluster. They are found in all passive clusters outside of the class starting areas. Once allocated, the player can choose a bonus from a list of thematically appropriate passive bonuses from the mastery to obtain. Allocating a mastery passive requires one skill point. The set of mastery passives offered are shared among their respective cluster categories, so for example a player can allocate a Fire Mastery from any of several Fire-related clusters, but the same mastery cannot be allocated twice.

entries.name: Ignite
entries.definition: Ignite is a damaging elemental ailment associated with fire that causes the affected target to take burning damage (fire damage over time).

entries.name: Imbalanced Guard
entries.definition: Imbalanced Guard is a keystone passive skill that doubles armour when defending against hits, but caps damage reduction to 50%.

entries.name: Immortal Ambition
entries.definition: Immortal Ambition is a keystone passive skill which allows life leech to recover energy shield while on full life, while disabling energy shield recharge and energy shield regeneration, and causing 5% energy shield loss per second.

entries.name: Immunity
entries.definition: Immunity is a stat that prevents and removes certain effects (e.g. debuffs or ailments) or nullifies certain damage types. Immunity is typically worded as either or .

entries.name: Impact
entries.definition: Impact is a notable Ascendancy passive skill for the Slayer that grants increased global accuracy rating, additional melee attack range, and increased area of effect per enemy killed recently. It also grants your melee attacks more damage the closer you are to an enemy.

entries.name: Impale
entries.definition: Impale is a mechanic that applies the Impaled debuff. Impaled enemies take reflected physical damage whenever they are hit, for a number of hits.

entries.name: Impending Doom Support
entries.definition: Impending Doom is a support gem for hex curses. When the hex on the supported skill expires, it triggers Doom Blast to deal chaos damage in an area around it. It cannot support curse skills which are triggered or applied as an aura with .

entries.name: Infernal Cry
entries.definition: Infernal Cry is a warcry skill gem that taunts nearby enemies, debuffs enemies to explode on death, buffs the user and allies to gain extra fire damage based on their physical damage, and exerts a number of subsequent attacks, causing those attacks to trigger the Combust attack.

entries.name: Influenced item
entries.definition: Influenced items are special types of base items with an expanded pool of exclusive modifiers, and are the only type of items that can obtain elevated modifiers. They can be recognized by their graphical effects and icon on the sides of the name plate. Influenced items are primarily dropped by influenced monsters and bosses. Certain unique items are influenced as well.

entries.name: Inspiration charge
entries.definition: Inspiration Charges are charges which are generated by using the . Currently it is the only source of the charge.

entries.name: Instant
entries.definition: Instant is a keyword that refers to skills with no use time, allowing them to be used without playing an animation or interrupting ongoing actions.

entries.name: Intelligence
entries.definition: The intelligence attribute is a measure of a character's knowledge and mental acuity. Intelligence is required to use intelligence-based equipment and skills.

entries.name: Intimidate
entries.definition: Intimidated is a debuff that causes the affected target to take 10% increased attack damage.

entries.name: Arcane Surge
entries.definition: Arcane Surge is a buff that grants bonus cast speed and mana regeneration.

entries.name: Chilling Area
entries.definition: A Chilling Area is a ground effect that causes enemies inside it to be ed. Chilled Ground, Creeping Frost, Frost Shield, and Vortices are Chilling Areas.

entries.name: Iron Grip
entries.definition: Iron Grip is a keystone passive skill that causes the physical damage bonus to melee attacks from strength to apply to projectile attacks as well.

entries.name: Iron Reflexes
entries.definition: Iron Reflexes is a keystone passive skill that converts all evasion rating into armour. It also removes the bonus to evasion rating that dexterity inherently grants.

entries.name: Link skill
entries.definition: Links are active skills that create a bond between your character and a specific party member, providing a benefit to them while they stay in range. If the target dies while linked, you will also die. Link skills cannot be triggered or used by Totems, Traps, or Mines.

entries.name: Iron Will
entries.definition: Iron Will is a keystone passive skill that causes the increased melee physical attack damage bonus from strength to apply to spells as well.

entries.name: Manifest Dancing Dervishes
entries.definition: Manifest Dancing Dervishes is a spell granted by . This spell summons two dancing dervish minions, while disabling the character's weapon. The character has Onslaught while the dancing dervishes remain alive.

entries.name: Item
entries.definition: Items in Path of Exile are used to represent not just a character's equipment but a variety of other game features. Items can be moved around between locations using the mouse cursor, including the inventory, worn items, stashes, and others, as well as on the ground. Not all types of items can be moved to all item locations. Different item types take a different amount of space in grid based item locations such as inventory and stashes.

entries.name: Triple damage
entries.definition: Triple damage is an effect that causes a hit to deal triple its damage. Triple damage overrides and does not stack with double damage.

entries.name: Covered in Frost
entries.definition: Covered In Frost is a debuff that causes the affected target to have less critical strike chance and increased cold damage taken.

entries.name: Item Quantity Support
entries.definition: Item Quantity is a support gem. It increases the quantity of items dropped by monsters killed by the supported skill. This skill gem no longer drops in the game, and can only be obtained by trading for existing ones in the permanent leagues. However, it can be found as a foil in the Legacy league through Reliquary Key.

entries.name: Item Rarity Support
entries.definition: Item Rarity Support is a support gem that increases the rarity of items dropped by monsters when they are killed using the supported skill.

entries.name: The Eater of Worlds
entries.definition: The Eater of Worlds is one of the Eldritch Horrors. Defeating the Eater of Worlds and the Searing Exarch and for the first time will drop an that can be socketed into the Atlas.

entries.name: The Searing Exarch
entries.definition: The Searing Exarch is one of the Eldritch Horrors. Defeating the Searing Exarch and the Eater of Worlds for the first time will drop an that can be socketed into the Atlas.
relatedTitles: List of searing exarch implicit modifiers

entries.name: Item socket
entries.definition: Item sockets are slots on equipment or resonators into which other items can be placed.

entries.name: Jewel
entries.definition: Jewels are items that can be placed into allocated jewel sockets in the passive skill tree, and can be removed or replaced at no cost. They grant certain buffs and abilities. Like most other items, jewels can be modified by orbs and are available in the four rarities. A rare jewel can have only four affixes instead of six.

entries.name: Karui
entries.definition: The Karui are a race/faction of the Wraeclast. They worship the Karui Gods and live in tribes amongst Karui Archipelago and Ngamakanui. The Karui were once slaves of Oriath.

entries.name: Keystone
entries.definition: A Keystone is a unique and powerful passive skill node that significantly impacts the way a character is played.

entries.name: Kill
entries.definition: Kill is a keyword that refers to causing the death of an enemy. Killing blow is a keyword that refers to hits that kill.

entries.name: Kinetic Blast
entries.definition: Kinetic Blast is an attack skill that fires a projectile from a wand, causing explosions around the location of the projectile's impact, dealing damage to enemies caught in their area of effect.

entries.name: Kineticism
entries.definition: Kineticism is a cluster jewel-only keystone passive skill that causes attack projectiles to always inflict Bleeding and Maim, as well as Knocking Back enemies, at the cost of being unable to pierce, fork, or chain.

entries.name: Kitava, the Insatiable
entries.definition: Kitava, the Insatiable is the final boss of Act 5 and Act 10. He is the main antagonist of The Fall of Oriath expansion. The battle consists of multiple phases in which players must damage Kitava, then damage Kitava's Heart, and this occurs alternatively until he is defeated.

entries.name: Knockback
entries.definition: Knockback is an on-hit effect that slightly pushes targets away from the attacker. Unlike a stun, a knockback does not interrupt the target's actions.

entries.name: Labyrinth enchantment
entries.definition: Labyrinth enchantments are a type of enchantment that used to be obtained from the Labyrinth. Completing the Labyrinth and interacting with the Divine Font in the final room would allow a piece of equipment to be imbued with a random enchantment. The eligible equipment types and the tier of the enchantment depended on the difficulty of the Labyrinth challenge. Each party member gained a use of the Divine Font upon completion of a lab if completed by a party.

entries.name: Leech
entries.definition: Leech recovers an amount of life, mana, or energy shield over time, relative to the damage inflicted on an enemy. Leech is based on the damage taken by the enemy, not the amount of life removed.

entries.name: Legion
entries.definition: Legions are ancient armies frozen in the midst of battle. They can be encountered by touching a Timeless Monolith, which breaks out the Legions and gives the player a window of time to defeat them. This encounter is considered Extra Content and has a baseline 8% chance to appear in any non-unique map area.

entries.name: Level
entries.definition: Level may refer to: * Character level (experience) * Skill gem level (gem experience) * Monster level * Item level * Drop level * Master level * Area level

entries.name: Life
entries.definition: Life (also called Health or Hit Points) is the health resource of a character or monster. For the player it is shown as a red orb in the lower left of the screen. Entities die when they reach 0 life and must resurrect in a town, hideout, or waypoint. Players can both lose and recover life in various ways, such as paying life costs of skills, taking damage, using flasks, regeneration, leech, among many other mechanics. Life is fully restored upon entering a town or hideout (except in Ruthless mode, which requires you to interact with certain NPCs).

entries.name: Life flask
entries.definition: Life flasks are an item class and a subtype of flasks which recovers life over time. The flask ends its effect if maximum Life is reached. They also queue up if multiple flasks are active.

entries.name: Sentinel
entries.definition: Sentinels are a league mechanic introduced in the Sentinel league. Sentinels can be activated to have them fire beams that empower a limited number of monsters and improve their item drops.

entries.name: Absorption charge
entries.definition: Absorption Charge is an alternative charge to . It is only granted from the 's mod . Players can generate them the same way they generate power charges.

entries.name: Light radius
entries.definition: Light radius is a stat which affects the maximum radius you can see clearly in low Light Level areas. Your light radius is further reduced by your current percentage of maximum life. This makes it very difficult to see in dark areas when on Low Life. An Energy Shield Mastery and Incandescent Heart changes your light radius to be based off your proportion of Energy Shield instead of life, aiding visibility for low life builds.

entries.name: Area
entries.definition: Area serves as generic term to describe any separately loaded zone in the game. Areas have various attributes and rule sets attributed them depending on the type of the area. Using the rules of the specific area the game creates a randomized time-limited instance of an area which can be played by the character.

entries.name: Lightning Arrow
entries.definition: Lightning Arrow is a bow attack skill that fires an arrow which causes enemies to be struck with a bolt of lightning. The lightning bolt can hit nearby enemies.

entries.name: Repeat
entries.definition: Repeating is a potential behaviour of skills. When you use a skill that repeats, you pay one cost and consume one cooldown, but perform the animation (and thus cause the effects of the skill) an additional time for each repeat.

entries.name: Lightning Strike
entries.definition: Lightning Strike is a melee strike attack skill that converts physical damage to lightning damage. It has a secondary effect where it launches projectiles that deal damage based on the player character's weapon damage with each swing.

entries.name: Eternal Empire
entries.definition: The Eternal Empire, or the Sarn Empire, is a faction of Wraeclast founded by the Azmeri, ruled by Emperors from its capital, Sarn. People who originate from this empire are known as "Eternals". Led by General Marceus Lioneye, is one of the factions that can be fought within the Domain of Timeless Conflict. The fallout of the Cataclysm resulted in the fall of the Eternal Empire. It was largely survived by the island of Oriath.

entries.name: Abyss
entries.definition: Abysses are interactable objects in instances which spawns cracks and pits that spawn monsters. They can spawn from Act 6 onwards. This encounter is considered Extra Content and has a baseline greater than 8% chance to appear in any map area.

entries.name: Lightning damage
entries.definition: Lightning damage is one of the five damage types and is one of the three types that count as elemental damage.

entries.name: Lingering blade
entries.definition: Lingering blades are created by certain skills and can be detonated with or animated with . Lingering Blades remain on the ground for a duration and can be used by specific skills. If Animated, they count as Daggers, and have the stats equivalent to a .

entries.name: Area of effect
entries.definition: Area of effect (often referred to as AoE) refers to mechanics (such as skills, auras, and monster abilities) that apply to an area of the ground (rather than targeting a particular character, monster, etc.).

entries.name: Unmodifiable
entries.definition: Unmodifiable is a property of certain items. An item that is unmodifiable cannot have any of its properties, base stats or modifiers altered by any means. The only exception is that an unmodifiable item can be identified. However, valid item bases can be used on the Recombinator to create a new item.

entries.name: Shatter
entries.definition: Monsters who are killed by hits while frozen shatter, leaving no corpse behind. Unique bosses cannot shatter. The on-death effects of many monsters will not occur if they are shattered, such as that of the Porcupine Goliath.
